lgpd.note: The ANPD recognised the EU and EEA in January 2026. The EU recognised Brazil the same day.

ukgdpr.note: Adequacy regulations, known as data bridges, under a data protection test.

fadp.note: Federal Council list of countries with adequate protection.

pdpa-ar.note: Transfers allowed to countries with adequate protection.

lpdp-uy.note: Transfers allowed to countries with adequate protection.

pipa-kr.note: The PIPC recognised the EU as equivalent in September 2025.

appi.note: Transfers allowed to countries designated as equivalent by the PPC.

nzpa.note: Transfer allowed where comparable safeguards exist. The Act also allows a list of prescribed countries.

popia.note: Transfer allowed where the recipient has adequate protection.

kdpa.note: Transfers to countries with adequate safeguards.

dpdp.note: Transfers allowed except to countries the government restricts.

ccpa.note: Service-provider contracts, but no SCC transfer regime.

lgpd.note: ANPD standard clauses, required for clause-based transfers since August 2025.

pipl.note: CAC standard contract, using the mandated CAC form.

ukgdpr.note: UK International Data Transfer Agreement or Addendum.

fadp.note: EU clauses recognized by the FDPIC, with Swiss adaptations.

lpdp-uy.note: Contractual clauses accepted, with URCDP authorisation.

pipa-kr.note: No standard-clause route. Contracts work only where necessary, with notice.

appi.note: Contractual measures ensure equivalent protection at the recipient.

nzpa.note: Contractual safeguards satisfy the transfer principle.

popia.note: Binding agreements with the recipient. The Regulator has issued no model clauses.

dpdp.note: No standard-contractual-clause regime; transfers turn on the country list.

ccpa.note: Not part of the CCPA framework.

lgpd.note: Global corporate rules, each approved by the ANPD.

fadp.note: Binding corporate rules approved by the FDPIC or an adequate country's authority.

pdpa-ar.note: AAIP guidelines for intra-group rules. Rules that depart from them need AAIP approval.

lpdp-uy.note: Group companies can share data under codes of conduct registered with the regulator. Little guidance is published.

appi.note: Intra-group rules can support equivalent protection.

nzpa.note: Intra-group safeguards can satisfy the transfer principle.

popia.note: Binding corporate rules are named in the Act.

kdpa.note: Binding corporate rules recognised since 2021, with ODPC approval.

pipl.note: Separate consent is required, but only alongside another transfer route.

fadp.note: A derogation for specific situations, with explicit consent.

pipa-kr.note: Separate consent required to transfer data abroad.

appi.note: Consent is the primary route for third-party transfer abroad.

nzpa.note: Allowed if you authorize it after being expressly told protections may be weaker.

dpdp.note: Consent underpins processing, but transfer turns on the country list.

ccpa.note: Not part of the CCPA framework.

fadp.note: Codes of conduct or certification can support transfers.

pdpa-ar.note: Not part of the transfer regime.

lpdp-uy.note: Not part of the transfer regime.

pipa-kr.note: A PIPC-designated certification held by the recipient can authorise a transfer.

appi.note: International certification can show the recipient has equivalent safeguards.

nzpa.note: Joining a prescribed binding scheme is one route.

popia.note: Not part of the transfer rule.

dpdp.note: Not part of the transfer model.

pipl.note: CAC security assessment for critical operators and large transfer volumes, with exemptions.

lpdp-uy.note: No security review, but the URCDP must authorise clause-based transfers to non-adequate countries.

pipa-kr.note: No general government pre-approval of transfers.

popia.note: Prior authorisation needed to send special or children's data to countries without adequate protection.

kdpa.note: Sensitive-data transfers may require confirmation of safeguards.

dpdp.note: No pre-approval; the government instead restricts specific countries.

pipl.note: Required for CIIOs and handlers above CAC volume thresholds.

kdpa.note: Six listed public-interest purposes, such as elections and health care, must use servers in Kenya.

dpdp.note: The government may require significant data fiduciaries to keep specified data in India. Sector rules can also apply.
